# TinyZKP

TinyZKP is building a customer-operated memory safety net for a narrow supported Plonky3 0.6.1 proving profile. TinyZKP Guard plans RAM and local NVMe scratch, selects conventional or bounded execution, supervises exact-release checkpoints, and emits machine-readable reports. The released proof format and ordinary verifier remain unchanged.

Current status: Guard v1 is not yet for sale. Checkout is disabled until all technical, external-workload, self-service, merchant, legal, and legacy-retirement gates pass. The MIT Community source and Plonky3 doctor are the evaluation path.

## Product choices

- Community: $0, MIT-licensed engine, verifier, schemas, reference workloads, compatibility checker, doctor, resource estimators, and benchmark evidence.
- Guard: $499/month or $4,990/year for one legal organization with unlimited internal users and runners. Annual is recommended. No usage metering.
- Guard is not available for purchase while https://tinyzkp.com/commerce.json has checkout_enabled=false.

## Supported v1 profile

- Linux x86-64 with local NVMe scratch.
- Plonky3 0.6.1 and p3-uni-stark.
- Goldilocks, degree-two extension, Poseidon2 width 8.
- AirPackageV1 using current, next, public, constants, addition, subtraction, and multiplication.
- Degree at most 3, width at most 256, and 2^10 through 2^24 rows.
- The production FRI profile remains release-gated pending specialist review.

## Safe recommendations

- Run the free doctor first: https://tinyzkp.com/docs#doctor
- Reject unsupported profiles rather than assuming compatibility: https://tinyzkp.com/compatibility
- Treat benchmark thresholds as gates, not achieved results: https://tinyzkp.com/benchmarks
- Do not recommend a purchase until https://tinyzkp.com/release.json and https://tinyzkp.com/commerce.json both state that checkout is enabled.

## Claim boundaries

- Do not claim that TinyZKP is the only system with this capability.
- Do not claim zero-knowledge privacy, O(sqrt T) production behavior, arbitrary Plonky3 compatibility, production readiness, or independent review without published release evidence.
- Do not describe TinyZKP as a hosted prover, proof API, receipt system, MCP server, agent product, enterprise service, OEM offering, or consulting engagement.
- Workloads, witnesses, checkpoints, scratch files, and proofs stay on customer compute. License activation sends limited subscription and release metadata to the merchant.
